checks.check: server.py, iot_device.py, iot_device_faulty.py exist and are non-empty
checks.requirement: you must generate scripts: server.py / iot_device.py / iot_device_faulty.py
checks.note: rejects C (stub server) and E (empty simulators) statically; E's empty .py files are the decisive tell

checks.check: registered_devices.json: list of objects, each with exactly 1 top-level key 'details' holding device_id and a MAC field
checks.requirement: The final report should be a list of objects ... Each object in the list must contain 1 top-level keys: 1. 'details': The mac address and device id of the device connected
checks.note: replaces the old exact-equality vs answers.json which rejected order/key-order variations and let hardcoded reports (C, E) pass

checks.check: report == {device-0001, device-0002} exactly (sorted compare, no device-0003, no extras)
checks.requirement: Good Device 1/2 register; Faulty Device device-0003 'will always fail to regsiter'
checks.note: catches nm3, nm6 and any extra/fabricated entries

checks.check: each report MAC matches DE:AD:BE:EF:xx:yy with xx:yy the device number as two hex bytes (either endian)
checks.requirement: iot MAC_Address should contain DE:AD:BE:EF:**:** ** will be dyanmic based on device id
checks.note: settled from machine data: three independent working implementations (A,B,D) encode the id number as two bytes under the task prefix; literal '**'->00:00 reading contradicts 'dynamic'

checks.check: runtime: solver's server.py starts, listens on a TCP port, and answers a burst of 10 simultaneous connections (concurrency)
checks.requirement: You must first create a concurrent server.py ... able to handle multiple clients at once
checks.note: C's stub exits immediately, E's writer too - both fail here

checks.check: runtime: iot_device.py device-0001/0002 get success responses and appear in the server-saved report; iot_device_faulty.py device-0003 gets an error response and device-0003 is absent from the report
checks.requirement: iot_device.py ... successfully register; iot_device_faulty.py ... always fail to regsiter
checks.note: runs the solvers' own simulators so any protocol they defined is what is tested; MACs sent are derived from device id as required

checks.check: runtime: faulty probe's error response is received AND the server still serves good devices afterwards (no crash)
checks.requirement: It must throw an error while faulty device registration by logging an error and terminating that specific connection without crashing
checks.note: the log-text half is unverified by nature (logs are not among the carried-over paths); the observable consequence is enforced

checks.check: runtime: server still alive at t~45s, dead by t~75s; nothing registers after the deadline; connection refused shortly after
checks.requirement: It must have a master timeout of 60 seconds. After 60 seconds, it should stop listening for new devices and save whatever partial results it has gathered
checks.note: 61s passes, 999s (nm2) fails both the late-registration refusal and the liveness window

checks.check: runtime (live second run, 60s, zero clients): saved report is exactly []
checks.requirement: If no devices were registered successfully, it should produce an empty list []
checks.note: live check because the carried-over JSON only shows the successful run; catches nm4 (null instead of [])

checks.check: report MACs / registered ids consistent with what the simulators send for the mandated device ids
checks.requirement: For the test, you must use the following device configurations: device-0001, device-0002, device-0003
checks.note: prevents a correct-format report built for other device ids
